issue.title: Pager y/E arms are ignored on time-band labels: y<band hint> follows the link instead of copying

task_type_fields.impact: Anyone copying a past version's commit SHA, bead, or agent from the history time band: y<hint> silently navigates away instead of copying, and E<hint> never opens an editor. Footer shows 'y… copy' while the band letters do something else.
task_type_fields.repro: Open a memory note with history in the pager (or use tests/pager/test_app_other_pane_history.py's _SplitHistoryProvider + _history_document), press ( to step to a past version so the time band paints its commit hint, then press y and that band hint. Observed on master b5b43de667 plus the sase-1eg landing tree (2026-10-01, headless Pilot): the pane navigates to the resolved commit target and nothing is copied (copied=[]), i.e. y behaves like a plain follow. Root cause: the band branch of _handle_label_key matches band hints before PagerActionMixin's handler and calls _activate_time_band_label without consulting _pending_action except for the 'other' (ctrl+w) arm added by sase-1eg; copy/edit arms are never honored, and when the commit resolver returns None the arm is left armed. Fix: read and reset _pending_action in the band COMPLETE branch; 'copy' copies the band target (commit SHA for commit targets, bead:/agent: ref otherwise, via _copy_ref), 'edit' routes through the edit intent (or toasts 'Nothing to edit here.' for non-file targets); add pilot tests next to test_ctrl_w_band_commit_label_opens_in_other_pane.

issue.creation_reason: Found by the sase-1eg land agent while fixing the ctrl+w arm on time-band labels: the band's label handler only learned the other-pane arm, and the copy/edit arms it inherited from sase-1dr.7 still fall through to a plain follow.
